- [FACT] Lyddie is described as a young girl living on a Vermont farm in the 1840s during the Industrial Revolution.
- [FACT] Lyddie’s father has abandoned the family, and her mother leaves her and her brother behind.
- [FACT] Lyddie is determined to hold on to her farm and works to pay off its debts.
- [EVENT] Lyddie decides to leave her job at Cutlers Tavern to work in the textile mills in Lowell, Massachusetts.
- [FACT] Lyddie is told by a customer at the tavern that she could earn at least two dollars a week at the mill and be independent.
- [CHANGE] Lyddie makes the choice to go to the mill to pay off her debts faster.
- [FACT] Lyddie starts making more money at the mill and buys a book, specifically "Oliver Twist."
- [FACT] Lyddie’s roommate at the mills is named Betsy.
- [FACT] Lyddie’s love for reading leads her to leave the farm again to attend Oberlin College in Ohio.
- [QUOTE] Lyddie states, “I’m off’ she said ‘to Ohio, there’s a college there that will take a women just like a man’” (p.181).
